intent: Get perspectives on the Q3 recovery pathway — auditor, customer-advocate, regulator views.

user_turns.text: I want auditor + customer-advocate + regulator perspectives on the parallel recovery.
Auditor would focus on the audit trail integrity during parallel ops.
Customer would focus on the friction during the campaign weeks.
Auditor says: parallel is fine if every change is logged + signed off. Concern: SDK fix + reactivation campaign creating overlapping change windows.
Customer-advocate says: 8 weeks of fix-then-campaign feels like 'getting bombarded with notices then asks for money.' Concern: tone.
Regulator says: SDK regression triggers reporting obligations. Concern: did we report on time?
Auditor + regulator perspectives BOTH point to reporting/audit trail — agreement. Customer-advocate is the outlier — focused on tone, not process.

output.triangulation_note: Auditor + regulator triangulate on process; customer-advocate spans differently to tone.

tensions.description: Process-side persons (auditor + regulator) tension against the customer-advocate's tone focus — the recovery plan has to satisfy BOTH but they pull different threads.

claims.text: Auditor-side view: parallel recovery is acceptable iff change-window logging is rigorous.
claims.confidence_rationale: Standard audit posture; high-conviction within the persona.

claims.text: Customer-advocate-side view: parallel recovery's tone-burden risks customer trust erosion if not paced.
claims.confidence_rationale: Persona-internal read; depends on campaign-team's tone discipline.

claims.text: Regulator-side view: SDK regression should trigger same-day report; recovery plan should include the regulator notice as workstream zero.
claims.confidence_rationale: Compliance posture is high-conviction within persona.

output.reflection_question: Of the persona's challenges, which is the one you find HARDEST to dismiss?
output.user_response: Regulator's — same-day reporting obligation may have been missed already. Need to check.
output.interpretation: User identifies a procedural gap surfaced by the regulator persona.

output.reflection_question: What's the question you wish you'd asked the persona but didn't?
output.user_response: Would have asked the auditor whether the parallel change windows would have looked OK if BOTH change owners signed off together OR if they need independent signoffs.

output.reflection_question: What other persona's view would change the picture again?
output.user_response: Engineering org chart — bringing in the on-call eng would surface what happens if a P0 fires during the parallel weeks.
output.interpretation: User opens an on-call-resilience persona for future Get Perspectives runs.

synthesis.body:
## Perspective spread

Three persons, three views. Two agree on process discipline (auditor + regulator); one diverges on customer-side tone (customer-advocate). The plan needs to satisfy both threads — rigour AND cadence.

## Where they tension

Process-side personas push the plan TOWARD more logging and earlier reporting. Customer-advocate pushes AWAY from overlapping touchpoints. The plan must thread both, not pick one.

recommendations.heading: Treat regulator notice as workstream zero
recommendations.body: Would issue the SDK regression regulator notice as workstream zero — the auditor + regulator persons both back this.

recommendations.heading: Cap customer-facing campaign touch-points
recommendations.body: Could cap customer-facing campaign touchpoints to ≤ 2 per week — the customer-advocate persona's primary concern.
